clue.text: Letter penned by Thatcher (not the heartless, batty old ruler)

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: pe is a letter of the Hebrew alphabet

indicators.note: not tells us to take a word away from the name before it
heartless strips the middle letter from the word the, leaving its two outer letters

parts.note: the word as written, before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: A letter written by Margaret Thatcher, with a parenthetical swipe at some dotty old ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' turns THE into TE; 'not' removes TE from THATCHER, leaving HATCHR; 'batty' scrambles PE with HATCHR. 'penned by' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptarch was one of the seven rulers of the Anglo-Saxon heptarchy, an old English kingdom system.

clue.text: Forced development here hurt both earl and duke

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Injuries to an earl and a duke, both aristocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a heated bed of soil where plants are forced, grown quickly ahead of season.

clue.text: Was mother honest about Oscar and daughter?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: pure means honest, untainted
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: A question whether a mother was truthful about Oscar and her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In British idiom 'to be mother' is to pour the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who serves tea at a table is said to be mother, so to pour it was to play mother.

clue.text: Apply initially after exercise, right, to stop soreness

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word
to stop means to plug a gap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pain is soreness
PE is physical exercise

explanation.surface: Advice to apply something after a workout to stop the aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apply' looks like part of the instructions but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain is to relate or belong, so it applies to something.

clue.text: Nick's traditional enemies bother showing up to do the job

parts.note: to nick is to cut
them and us are the traditional opposing camps

indicators.note: showing up in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: drat is an exclamation of annoyance, like bother

explanation.surface: Nick's old foes don't bother turning up for work.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet the required standard is an idiom for coping well, doing the job adequately.

clue.text: Bishop admitting moon I caught on film

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: BP is the abbreviation for bishop
Io is a moon of Jupiter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bishop confesses he caught sight of the moon, perhaps while filming.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, a life story told on film.

clue.text: Day I flipped over love letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: flipped over means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday

explanation.surface: One day the speaker fell head over heels in love with some letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the Greek letter i, so iotas are letters, also tiny amounts.

clue.text: Emptied pot over me in a rage — it smells horrible!

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: in a rage means wild, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone furious empties a pot over the speaker, and it reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a rage' looks like one phrase, but 'in a' is fodder and 'rage' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are foul-smelling compounds produced when protein rots.

clue.text: Natural sprinters … like Johnson and Gatlin, say?

indicators.note: say signals the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the sprinters Ben Johnson and Justin Gatlin were both banned for doping, so cheaters

explanation.surface: Born sprinters, like the famous runners Johnson and Gatlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Johnson and Justin Gatlin are Olympic sprinters with doping bans.
explanation.definitionFit: These big cats are the fastest land animals, sprinters by nature.

clue.text: Loud sound from bottom — what was offensive about it?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was the 1968 Vietnam campaign
the rump is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: A crude joke about a loud noise emerging from someone's backside, and what was rude about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thoughts of breaking wind; 'offensive' is really the Tet Offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is a loud brass call, and the word also means any loud blaring noise.

clue.text: Deep trouble on the way?

parts.note: read literally, a deep hole that causes trouble on the road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep trouble' sounds like serious difficulty ahead; it is literally a deep hole in the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hole that jolts cars is literally a deep source of trouble along the way.

clue.text: Pat halted orgy, in order to ____ ?

definitions.text: Pat halted orgy, in order to ____ ?

indicators.note: put in order means the letters are rearranged into the right sequence

explanation.surface: Pat stops an orgy, and we are invited to fill in why.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer: Pat broke off the orgy to seem less available.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning reluctance to seem more desirable is the coy tactic the phrase names.

clue.text: Three men hold back Arab leader

indicators.note: back tells us to read the hidden letters in reverse
the words Three men hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Three men restrain the leader of an Arab group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' points to letters inside 'thREE MEn', and 'back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim ruler or chieftain in the Arab world.

clue.text: Spin result, maybe cutting advantage

parts.note: heads is one result of spinning a coin
a cutting remark is tart, sharp

explanation.surface: The result of a coin toss might reduce someone's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a head start gives an early lead, an advantage over the field.

clue.text: Fight with male judges and don't get picked to perform …

parts.note: a war is a fight
the bench is a collective term for judges

explanation.surface: A man fighting with the judiciary and not being selected for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitutes who sit on the sidelines all match and never play are said to sit idle as reserves, an idiom.

clue.text: Many bones broken? Definitely not

indicators.note: broken means smashed, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: Asked whether many bones are broken, the answer is a firm no.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic negative, certainly not.

clue.text: Posh occasionally: 'I'm last to perform for David?'

indicators.note: occasionally means take every other letter
to perform suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Posh Spice saying she is last on stage for David Beckham.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh and David suggest the Beckhams; David is the biblical king credited with the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms, so he was a writer of sacred songs.

clue.text: Ship and train — he fiddled both in short

indicators.note: both says the shortening applies to each of the two words

parts.note: to school is to train

indicators.note: in short means cut off at the end

parts.note: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A ship and a train, both fiddled by someone, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both in short' cuts the last letter from SCHOOL and NERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts.

clue.text: … as these may do in next series

parts.note: second means next in order
a string is a series, as in a string of wins

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the people who do that might do it in the next series.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue: reserve players are the ones who sit on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-string players are reserves, the very people who sit out the game unpicked.

clue.text: Sheep in main road is right little madam

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: the A1 is a main road in Britain, its 1 read as I
a gal is a girl, a little madam

explanation.surface: A sheep is in the main road, and so is a cheeky little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The argali is a wild Asian mountain sheep with huge curling horns.

clue.text: Dismissing driver's warning, soon fit in

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a piece is removed

parts.note: before long means soon
fore is the golfer's warning shout after driving a ball

explanation.surface: A motorist ignoring a warning will soon get the hang of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is a golfer, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to fit in somewhere, to be accepted.

clue.text: Tramp's unlikely to step on it

definitions.meaning: a scruffy vagrant is unlikely to appear well dressed
step on it means hurry up, be quick about it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to appear well dressed and, in British usage, to hurry up.

clue.text: Alert teacher at Eton to truanting

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher

indicators.note: truanting means absent, so these letters go missing

explanation.surface: Warning a teacher at Eton about a pupil skipping class.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alarm, a device that gives an alert.

clue.text: Join German in pool

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mere is a pool or small lake

explanation.surface: An invitation to swim with a German in a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or join together.

clue.text: New setter looks embarrassed about being passed over

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to go red is to look embarrassed

explanation.surface: A new compiler blushes about being overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignored means being disregarded, passed over without notice.

clue.text: Animal droppings Bill steps in

indicators.note: steps in means enters, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An animal's droppings that someone called Bill treads in.
explanation.definitionFit: The guanaco is a South American camelid, a wild relative of the llama.

clue.text: Mob beginning to riot — not much cover outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a thong is skimpy underwear or swimwear that covers little

indicators.note: beginning to means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A mob starting to riot, with scantily dressed people out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd of people, a mob.

clue.text: Setting by design hits snag

indicators.note: by design suggests a deliberate rearrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An arrangement deliberately hits a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' belongs to the definition: setting by means putting aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing is hoarding or putting away for later, which is what setting by means.
